newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FNB to sell troubled FirstPref division.
newsitem.headline: FNB to sell troubled FirstPref division.

text.p: First National Bank Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it had agreed to sell its FirstPref unit to McCarthy Retail Ltd by March 31, 1997.
It said in a statement that the current arrangements relating to the financing of McCarthy's business had not worked out to the mutual benefit of both companies as originally envisaged.

"Accordingly, it has been decided that FNB will sell FirstPref to McCarthy Retail after having transferred to a new company all its (FirstPref's) other customers, notably Profurn Ltd and other independent retailers," the statement said.
It said these other customers were operating well.

A preferable arrangement, which was likely to be similar to that in place between FNB and McCarthy prior to the sale of FirstPref to FNB in 1995, would again be put in place. Details of this would be announced when finalised, before March 31, 1997.
The statement said the new arrangement would have some impact on FNB's interim earnings, although this would not be significant over the financial year.
The sale was not likely to have a material effect on the headline earnings of McCarthy for the year ended June 30, 1997.

FNB said the new scheme would be highly beneficial to both parties. FNB's total assets would not be negatively affected as the bank would continue to provide finance to McCarthy and enjoy the future earnings from this source.
The effective date of the transfer would be April 1, 1997.
The bad debt warranty granted to FirstPref by McCarthy would fall away with effect from March 31, 1997.
FNB last month reported a meagre eight percent rise in headline earnings to 229.8 cents a share in the year to September 30, well below analysts expectations.
The bottomline was particularly hard hit by a 69 percent surge in bad debts with instalment financiers FirstPref and Wesbank the biggest culprits.
